question.text: This Irish political figure avoided being executed following the Easter Rising, and opposed the Anglo-Irish Treaty; he would later serve as President of Ireland until his death in 1975.
question.clue: This leader's American citizenship allowed him to escape execution after the Easter Rising.

swap.leadin: Taoiseach [pr. TEA-SHICH] Brian Cowen, the prime minister of this nation, was incriminated in 2009 after revelations that this country's central bank had hidden millions of euros worth of loans.
swap.text: Name this country which was partitioned in two in 1920, then declared a "Free State" two years later.
swap.clue: A civil war erupted in this country between pro and anti-treaty forces led by Michael Collins and Eamon de Valera, respectively.

question.leadin: It was led by Patrick Pearse and Tom Clarke.
question.text: Name this 1916 revolt in which rebels took over the General Post Office and other buildings until they were defeated and executed by the British. William Butler Yeats wrote a poem about this event.
question.answerHtml: Easter Rising [accept Easter Rebellion, or anything else involving people revolting and Easter]
question.clue: That participant, Patrick Pearse, was part of a group that took over locations such as Boland's Bakery and Jacob's Biscuit Factory, though it was centered in the General Post Office.

swap.text: Domestically, Blair negotiated this agreement, which released IRA prisoners and ended the Troubles.
swap.clue: Bertie Ahern and David Andrews were signatories of this document, which was primarily negotiated by David Trimble and John Hume.

question.leadin: Two militants were shot at a Gibraltar gas station as part of Operation Flavius during this conflict.
question.text: Name this conflict ended by the Good Friday Agreement. Paramilitaries such as the Provisional IRA and the Ulster Volunteer Force were active during this conflict.
question.answerHtml: the Troubles [prompt on, but do NOT otherwise reveal, the Northern Ireland conflict or Northern Irish conflict]
question.clue: The Sunningdale Agreement was a failed peace attempt during this conflict.

swap.text: This paramilitary organization tried to assassinate Thatcher in the Brighton Hotel bombing. During her term, a member of this group, Bobby Sands, died from a hunger strike in Maze Prison.
swap.clue: This group placed a bomb inside a fishing boat that killed the last Viceroy of India, Lord Mountbatten, and a member of this organization named Bobby Sands became a martyr after dying during a hunger strike.

question.leadin: The Annals of the Four Masters describe an event in which unpaid longshoremen in this city refused to help move barrels of gunpowder off of English boats. Shockingly, they exploded.
question.text: Name this city where Sigtrygg Silkbeard was defeated by the forces of Brian Boru at the Battle of Clontarf. Lord Frederick Cavendish and Thomas Henry Burke were stabbed to death in a park in this city.
question.clue: This city is named for a black tidal pool where the River Poddle meets the River Liffey.

swap.text: The murders killed momentum for the movement to grant this status of self-government to Ireland. This two-word term names four bills in favor of Irish autonomy that successive Liberal governments failed to pass.
swap.answerHtml: Irish home rule [reject partial answers, prompt on ‘autonomy’]
swap.clue: Edward Carson and James Craig, leaders of the Unionists, campaigned against a 1914 bill aiming to bring about this outcome.

question.leadin: The Freeman's Journal was his major organ of support, and his political career ended when that newspaper switched allegiances.
question.text: Name this Irish advocate and member of the British parliament, who had earlier weathered alleged involvement in the "Phoenix Park murders."
question.clue: The shortcomings of the Land Act of 1881 prompted him to join the opposition to William Gladstone, with whom he had negotiated the Kilmainham Agreement a year later.

swap.leadin: Name these members of the Irish Republican Army.
swap.text: This IRA intelligence director worked with Arthur Griffith to negotiate the 1921 treaty creating the Irish Republic, though IRA hardliners were dissatisfied with the terms.
swap.clue: This leader of an assassination group known as The Squad was imprisoned at Frongoch internment camp for their role as aide-de-camp to Joseph Plunkett during the Easter Rising.

question.text: This member of the IRA was elected as a member of Parliament while he was in prison. He died in Maze Prison less than a month after his election as part of the 1981 Irish hunger strike.
question.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.

swap.text: The collapse of Stormont was precipitated by the resignation of this Sinn Fein politician, who served as Deputy First Minister under the DUP leaders Peter Robinson and Arlene Foster and died shortly after his resignation.

question.leadin: Daisen Kofun, the largest example of one of these structures in Japan, is shaped like a key-hole.
question.text: Name these structures exemplified by Newgrange in Ireland. In the UK, these structures are known as barrows.
question.answerHtml: burial mounds [accept passage grave or passage tombs; accept tumuli or tumulus; accept BUT DO NOT OTHERWISE REVEAL kurgans]
question.clue: The largest "platform" example of these structures in North America is the "Monks" one in Illinois.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about David Ricardo's worst nightmare--the Corn Laws.
swap.text: The Corn Laws began to be repealed with the onset of this event, which lasted from 1845 to around 1850 and had its effects worsened by the Gregory clause. Many then emigrated from the Emerald Isle to countries like the U.S.
swap.clue: The Baring Brothers and Company ordered shipments of corn in response to this event, but other relief efforts were stopped by Charles Trevelyan, who attributed this event to divine judgment.

question.leadin: Answer the following about British-Irish conflict.
question.text: Mostly comprised of World War I veterans, this temporary British constabulary unit was loathed for their brutal treatment of Irish civilians, as in the Croke Park massacre.
question.clue: Lyrics by Dominic Behan invite these people to "show your wives how you won medals down in Flanders."

swap.leadin: One part of this event saw the raising of republican flags over the General Post Office.
swap.text: Name this failed rebellion by Sinn Fein lead by Patrick Pearse and James Connolly to establish an independent Ireland that took place during the eponymous week.
swap.clue: This poem in which William Butler Yeats memorializes "MacDonagh and MacBride / and Connolly and Pearse," who were killed as a result of an uprising.

question.leadin: Settlers in this region included wealthy "Undertakers" and war veterans called "Servitors."
question.text: Name this region whose "plantation" during James I's reign began after a failed rebellion in the Nine Years' War. The "Flight of the Earls" from this region marked the end of its old order.
question.answerHtml: Ulster [or Ulaidh or Cúige Uladh or Ulstèr; accept “Plantation of Ulster”; prompt on Ireland or Éire or Airlann]
question.clue: This province was the site of an early 17th century "plantation," in which James I settled thousands of Scots here.

swap.leadin: This battle began with a feigned retreat as the vikings of Sigurd of Orkney pretended to leave in their longboats, but instead slipped around the Munster army and disembarked in the morning.
swap.text: Identify this 1014 battle fought outside of Dublin.
swap.clue: Ulf the Quarrelsome, a prolific skull cup creator and user, allegedly killed Brodir of Man by wrapping his entrails around a tree at this battle. At this battle, the Irish under Brian Boru soundly defeated a Viking force.

question.leadin: Name these sources which document the extreme weather events of 535 to 536 C.E., the most significant global cooling in the past 2,000 years.
question.text: This set of annals documents the frigid weather of the 530s as well as many other severe climate events over centuries of Irish history. These annals were compiled by monks on a namesake island in the Lakes of Killarney.

swap.leadin: Name these things related to the Irish Home Rule movement in the late 19th-century, FTP each.
swap.text: Parnell was initially accused of involvement in the May 1882 murders of Lord Cavendish and his undersecretary in this Dublin location. The murders had been carried out by the nationalist terrorist group The Invincibles.
swap.clue: On May 6, 1882 surgical knives were used to off Burke and his boss Lord Frederick Cavendish at this site that now gives the grisly event its name.
